cards.explanation: The answer is False. The LORD says, "I have loved you with an everlasting love…" (Jeremiah 31:3) No fine print, no "while supplies last," no little stamp on the bottom. Love that never ends is why He draws them close.

The answer is that He will rebuild her. The LORD says, "Again I will build you, and you will be rebuilt, O Virgin Israel." (Jeremiah 31:4) I know a little about being made new after years in the back of a junk drawer. Being rebuilt feels GOOD, friends.

The answer is that she will go out in joyful dancing. "Again you will take up your tambourines and go out in joyful dancing." (Jeremiah 31:4) The tambourines are coming out for a party. That's a lot of jingling, and every bit of it is joyful.
The answer is True. The verse says, "the farmers will plant and enjoy the fruit." (Jeremiah 31:5) The ones who plant are the ones who enjoy it. That's a promise worth a little dance, bakers.

The answer is to go up to Zion to the LORD. The watchmen call out, "Arise, let us go up to Zion, to the LORD our God!" (Jeremiah 31:6) It's a call to come together and head toward the LORD. Hollering from a hilltop for that is a fine use of lungs, friends.
The word is "save." The LORD says to say, "O LORD, save Your people, the remnant of Israel!" (Jeremiah 31:7) It's a prayer, and the LORD is the one who puts the words in their mouths.

The answer is False. God says He will gather them "…including the blind and the lame, expectant mothers and women in labor." (Jeremiah 31:8) The trip home isn't a tryout, friends. There's no fitness test at the door.

The answer is a level path where they won't stumble. God says, "I will make them walk beside streams of waters, on a level path where they will not stumble." (Jeremiah 31:9) I think that's exactly what a crowd with the blind and the lame in it needs. A flat road is a kind road, bakers.

The word is "Father." God says, "For I am Israel’s Father, and Ephraim is My firstborn." (Jeremiah 31:9) Father and firstborn are family words, friends. So God speaks about Ephraim the way a dad speaks about his firstborn.

The answer is as a shepherd keeps his flock. "The One who scattered Israel will gather them and keep them as a shepherd keeps his flock." (Jeremiah 31:10) The same One who scattered is the One who gathers. And He keeps them the way a shepherd keeps his flock.

The answer is False. They "…will be radiant over the bounty of the LORD…" and the verse adds, "…never again will they languish." (Jeremiah 31:12) That's the opposite of scraping by, friends. It's more than enough.

The answer is a well-watered garden. God says, "Their life will be like a well-watered garden, and never again will they languish." (Jeremiah 31:12) To languish is to droop and wither. A garden with plenty of water is the picture He picks for their life back home, bakers.

The answer is joy. God says, "I will turn their mourning into joy, and give them comfort and joy for their sorrow." (Jeremiah 31:13) The mourning gets turned into joy, friends. And for their sorrow, He gives comfort and joy.

The answer is because they are no more. The verse says, "…Rachel weeping for her children and refusing to be comforted, because they are no more." (Jeremiah 31:15) I think this is one of the heavy parts of the passage, friends. It's a mother's grief, and the text lets it be that.

The answer is True. The LORD tells Rachel, "Then your children will return from the land of the enemy." (Jeremiah 31:16) The weeping gets an answer, friends. He doesn't tell her to stop crying and leave it there.

The word is "hope." The LORD says, "So there is hope for your future, declares the LORD, and your children will return to their own land." (Jeremiah 31:17) After all that weeping, hope gets the last word in this part, bakers.

The answer is that Ephraim asks God to restore him so he can return. Ephraim says, "Restore me, that I may return, for You are the LORD my God." (Jeremiah 31:18) He asks to be restored so he can return, friends. And the reason he gives is that the LORD is his God.

The answer is True. Ephraim says, "I was ashamed and humiliated because I bore the disgrace of my youth." (Jeremiah 31:19) He owns it out loud, which is not an easy thing to do. I think that takes real guts, friends.

The answer is that God remembers him. God says, "Though I often speak against him, I still remember him." (Jeremiah 31:20) Speaking against him and remembering him both happen in the same breath, bakers. And God goes on to say His heart yearns for Ephraim.

The answer is to return to her own cities. The verse says, "Return, O Virgin Israel, return to these cities of yours." (Jeremiah 31:21) Those are her own cities, friends. Right before that comes the instruction, "Set up the road markers, put up the signposts."

The word is "wander." The LORD asks, "How long will you wander, O faithless daughter?" (Jeremiah 31:22) Just before that, He says, "Set up the road markers, put up the signposts." (Jeremiah 31:21) Then comes the question about wandering, friends.

The answer is a blessing. The people will say, "May the LORD bless you, O righteous dwelling place, O holy mountain." (Jeremiah 31:23) After the captivity, the land hears blessings again, friends. That's a good sound.

The word is "weary." God says, "…I will refresh the weary soul and replenish all who are weak." (Jeremiah 31:25) If you've ever dragged yourself to the end of a long week, you know what weary feels like, bakers. That's the kind of soul He says He will refresh.

The answer is False. The one speaking says, "At this I awoke and looked around. My sleep had been most pleasant to me." (Jeremiah 31:26) The sleep is called most pleasant, not troubled, friends. The passage closes on that note.
